newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo says Gyll leaves, Johansson new MD.
newsitem.headline: Volvo says Gyll leaves, Johansson new MD.

text.p: Swedish vehicle manufacturer Volvo AB said on Monday Soren Gyll was to leave the position of managing director from April 23.
The company said in a statement that he will be replaced by Leif Johansson, currently chief executive of Swedish appliance maker Electrolux.
Volvo said Gyll informed the board that he wished to leave his executive position at the annual general meeting of the company on April 23.
Volvo chairman, Bert-Olof Svanholm, said the company regretted Gyll's decision, saying Volvo has undergone great and positive changes during Gyll's five years at the top.
He said Volvo was pleased that Gyll had expressed his willingness to remain on the company's board.
Gyll said in a statement that Volvo's goal of becoming exclusively a transport equipment group has essentially been implemented and the group was strong, financially as well as product wise.
"The group now faces a number of important strategic and structural decisions that will have consequences extending far into the future and whose implementation will demand continuity," Gyll said.
"It is against this background and since I had, in any event, intended to relinquish my executive duties next year at age 58, that I consider this is the proper time to pass the baton.

"Moreover after 16 years in chief executive position in large publicly listed companies, it feels natural to want to create another environment and devote more time to my family and personal interests."
His successor, Johansson, who was born in 1951, joined Electrolux in 1984 and has been president since 1991 and chief executive officer since 1994, the statement said.
